Krakow Podgorze New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kraków-Podgórze, Poland

Demolished. This cemetery's land was purchased by the Jewish community of Kraków between 1919 and 1921 and officially opened in 1932. In the fall of 1942, the Germans established a forced labor camp at Płaszów on the site, converting it into a concentration camp in 1944; forced laborers were made to tear out the cemetery's own tombstones to pave the camp's roads, and barracks, an assembly square, and a water reservoir were built directly on the grounds. The Chevra Kadisha building was used to house SS officers and as a prison; the funeral house served as a stable before its 1944 demolition. In 2003, a matzevah was erected nearby for Sara Schenirer, founder of the Beis Yaakov Orthodox girls' education movement.
